cues: Nouns whose number is not what it looks.
Subjects and diseases ending in s are singular: mathematics is easy; measles is serious.
Two part tools and clothes are plural: the scissors are blunt; but a pair of scissors is missing.
Police, cattle and people are plural without an s. Titles, countries and organisations are singular: the United States is a federal republic.
An amount of money, time or distance is one amount: twenty rupees is not much; five years is a long time.
A committee acting as one body is singular.
The plus an adjective, the rich, is plural.
And a gerund or infinitive subject is singular: swimming is good exercise; to err is human.
